title: Why Anthropic Stock Is Up (and Down) Today
summary: Anthropic, PBC (NASDAQ:ANT) stock is finally trading, opening at $111.50, up more than 34% from its $83 initial public offering (IPO) price. It has since dropped, however, falling roughly 17% from its open price to $93.10 as of 1:20 p.m. ET on Thursday, Nov. 19. The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) and the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) are both down 1.6%. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » On Wednesday, the maker of the Claude AI models sold 980 million shares at $83 apiece. That was well above the $70 to $78 range it had marketed. That initially valued Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis -- counting all the shares that could eventually exist. That makes nearly as large as Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA)and Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META). Revenue hit $16.96 billion in the third quarter, up an incredible 47% from the prior quarter. But Anthropic is still running at a loss on an operating basis and has already committed to spending about $895 billion -- roughly half of that is promised by 2030. If revenue keeps growing like this, that might not be a problem, but I'm not sure that pace can hold, and at this valuation there isn't much room for a slowdown -- which may already be happening . While 47% sequential growth is certainly incredible, that's actually significantly slower than the previous sequential jump.
